descriptions: Brahman is one as cause and many as effect; the world and souls are its real transformations (pariṇāma) through its power (śakti).
Bhāskara: difference from the soul is due to real adjuncts (upādhi), non-difference is natural.
Yādavaprakāśa: Brahman is naturally both one and many, transforming into Īśvara, the souls and matter.
Vijñānabhikṣu: souls and prakṛti are non-separate (avibhāga) from Brahman, which is their substrate.
negations: Denies that the world is an illusory appearance (vivarta) of Brahman.
Denies that difference is merely imagined through a positive avidyā.
relation_to_self: The soul is a part (aṃśa) of Brahman, limited by real adjuncts (Bhāskara) or naturally distinct-yet-one (Yādava); at liberation, after death, it becomes non-different from Brahman.
relation_to_world: The world is Brahman's real effect and is non-different from it as cause; it is neither false nor wholly other.
caveat: The school would reject a one-truth reading that treats its difference as merely provisional; for Bhāskara the adjuncts that make the difference are real until death.

descriptions: By nature free of every fault, the single mass of all auspicious qualities, having the vyūhas as his limbs (Daśaślokī 4).
Worshipped with Rādhā, daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, on his left, served by thousands of sakhīs (Daśaślokī 5).
Both material and efficient cause through his powers; the controller of cit and acit, which are naturally different and non-different from him.
negations: Denies that difference is due to adjuncts.
relation_to_self: The soul is an atomic knower, part of the Lord, dependent on him, different and non-different by nature; liberated, it attains his nature without losing its distinctness.
relation_to_world: The world is real, a transformation of the Lord's power; acit is prākṛta, aprākṛta or time.
caveat: The school holds its dual-and-non-dual relation to be natural and eternal; it would reject a reading that collapses it into identity or into sheer difference.

descriptions: The locus of contradictory attributes (viruddha-dharmāśraya): with and without qualities, moving and unmoving.
Puruṣottama is the highest; Akṣara Brahman is his abode and the goal of knowers; Antaryāmin dwells within.
Madhurāṣṭaka: everything of the lord of sweetness is sweet.
negations: Denies that māyā has any part in Brahman or in the world's reality (against Śaṅkara's māyāvāda).
relation_to_self: The soul is a spark-like part (aṃśa) of Brahman in which bliss (ānanda) is concealed by the Lord's will; by grace it is manifested in service.
relation_to_world: The world is Brahman itself, transformed without change (avikṛta-pariṇāma); real and to be honoured; only saṃsāra — the soul's 'I and mine' — is unreal.
caveat: The impersonal Akṣara is held lower than Puruṣottama; Puṣṭimārga would reject any equalising of the knower's Brahman and the devotee's Kṛṣṇa.

names.name: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya (Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa combined)

descriptions: The non-dual reality is called Brahman, Paramātman and Bhagavān (BhP 1.2.11); Bhagavān is its full manifestation.
Kṛṣṇa is the supreme Lord, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, beginningless, the origin and cause of all causes (Brahma Saṃhitā 5.1).
The possessor of inconceivable powers (acintya-śakti), related to them in inconceivable difference-and-non-difference.
Rasa itself; most fully manifest in Vraja with Rādhā, his hlādinī-śakti.
negations: The impersonal Brahman is the effulgence of his body (Brahma Saṃhitā 5.40), an incomplete manifestation, not the highest.
Denies that his form is a product of māyā or that the world is vivarta.
relation_to_self: The soul is the Lord's marginal power (taṭasthā-śakti), an eternal servant, one with and different from him inconceivably (CC 2.20.108).
relation_to_world: The world is a real but temporary transformation of his external power (māyā-śakti); he himself remains unchanged, like the wish-fulfilling gem.
caveat: Gauḍīyas accept the three names of BhP 1.2.11 but grade them (Bhagavān fullest); they reject any reading that makes the personal form a provisional appearance of an impersonal Absolute.

names.name: Paramākāśa / dahara (the supreme ether in the heart)

descriptions: Śiva endowed with cit-śakti, free from all defects, the material and efficient cause of the world.
The supreme ether of the Upaniṣads is his śakti; he is to be meditated on in the small space of the heart.
negations: Denies an attributeless Brahman without śakti.
Denies that Śiva is only the efficient cause.
relation_to_self: Souls (paśu) are his body and attribute, distinct yet inseparable; liberated, they become equal to Śiva in bliss (śiva-sāmya) but not identical.
relation_to_world: The world is real, a manifestation of the subtle world held in Śiva's śakti.
caveat: Appayya Dīkṣita read the school as a step towards Advaita; the school's own text and its Vīraśaiva heirs hold the qualified non-dualism as final.
